rationale: Re-derived at 953e9abb, lens contract stability. Round-1 F1/F1b/F2/F3 classification: F1 RESOLVED for the default configuration — ComputeEntangleablePaths now derives the recording class per-spec and the .gitignore class per-state, and I ran the mandated recording-enabled pin live (TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_EnumerationPin_RecordingEnabled, PASS in 141s, a real bd+git claim whose porcelain diff exactly matches the prediction, len==2 sanity included). F1b RESOLVED — the pin leg is exactly what I asked for and it is honest (real subprocess claim, real diff, exact match). F2 RESOLVED BEYOND MY ASK — the .gitignore class makes the enumeration genuinely non-empty, so the refusal now has REAL e2e coverage: all four porcelain-shape variants (modified/deleted/renamed-away/symlinked) run the actual binary, assert 'cannot claim work', and prove byte-identical no-op (PASS, 381s). F3 RESOLVED beyond the wording nit — the presence bit is consumed and present-but-invalid is a fourth distinguished no-op outcome that refuses to guess over a corrupt value. I also verified: claimAnchorRoot is a faithful replica of MindspecExecutor.resolveAnchorRoot (identical SpecWorktreePath+os.Stat logic, both honoring cfg.WorktreeRoot); parsePorcelainZ's rename field order (NEW then ORIG) matches real git -z output, which I reproduced in a scratch fixture; HasGitignoreEntry is the literal check EnsureGitignoreEntry now calls, so divergence is structurally impossible; StatusZWithStderr's separate-streams rationale is sound. HOWEVER, the brief's core question — 'is the workspace.SpecDir worktree-preference the fix replicates the same one recording.EventsPath resolves through? any config where they diverge?' — has answer NO / YES-THEY-DIVERGE: recording paths resolve through workspace.SpecDir, whose worktree probe uses DefaultWorktreesDir(root) with a NIL config (worktree.go:114-116 → hardcoded '.worktrees'), while claimAnchorRoot resolves through SpecWorktreePath(root, cfg, specID) honoring cfg.WorktreeRoot (a supported, containment-validated config knob, config.go:568-588). Under a custom worktree_root the two anchors disagree and the recording class silently disarms exactly where the write actually lands (G-r2-1). A second same-seam gap: the samePath(anchor, cwd) gate compares cwd LITERALLY, but porcelain paths are toplevel-relative (verified empirically: git -C <subdir> status --porcelain reports repo-root-relative paths), so invoking next from a subdirectory of the anchor tree — supported by workspace.FindRoot and the spec-079 location-agnostic posture — disarms every class in the DEFAULT config while the dirt is fully observable and the writes land in that very tree (G-r2-2). And the guard's own doc block still carries the first-draft's falsehood ('ALWAYS write under repoRoot... does NOT route through resolveAnchorRoot', 'the recording class when repoRoot == cwd') directly contradicting both the code and the corrected comment thirty lines below (G-r2-3). The fix's load-bearing equivalence claim is false outside the default config, so this is a genuine RC, not a nit — but the failure modes are conditional false negatives (fail-open to a notice, never a wrongful block), the default config is e2e-verified sound, and one coherent change closes all three, so no hard block.
concrete_changes_required: G-r2-1 (major): Close the SpecDir/SpecWorktreePath anchor divergence. recording.EventsPath/ManifestPath resolve via workspace.SpecDir, whose worktree probes (workspace.go:484-492) join DefaultWorktreesDir(root) — nil cfg, hardcoded '.worktrees' — while claimAnchorRoot honors cfg.WorktreeRoot. With a custom worktree_root configured, recording enabled, and a spec worktree present: SpecDir misses the worktree and resolves to the ROOT checkout's spec dir, so the claim's recording write lands under repoRoot — yet a claim invoked FROM repoRoot has anchor==customWt != cwd, the recording class is excluded, and a pre-dirty manifest.json at repoRoot is read-modify-written after being waved through as ignoredDirt. That is round-1 F1's exact failure, resurrected in a supported configuration. (SpecDir's worktree probes also cover only flat/canonical shapes, never the legacy step-5 shape — same divergence mechanism for legacy-shaped trees.) Preferred fix, which also closes G-r2-2: stop replicating resolution logic — gate each class on the RESOLVED write target itself. Resolve EventsPath/ManifestPath (and the .gitignore anchor) to absolute paths, compute them relative to the TOPLEVEL of cwd's working tree (git rev-parse --show-toplevel, or the existing worktree-context helpers), and include the class iff the relative path does not escape ('..'). Then the gate is true by construction whenever the write is observable, no matter which helper resolved it. Acceptable fallback: make SpecDir cfg-aware (or add a cfg-taking variant the recording package uses) plus a pinned test with a custom worktree_root; if instead the residual is accepted, the guard comment must say so explicitly and a follow-up bead must be filed for SpecDir's nil-cfg probe (that defect predates this bead and mis-targets recording WRITES generally under custom worktree_root, not just this guard).

G-r2-2 (minor): Fix the cwd-vs-toplevel base. samePath(anchor, cwd) and filepath.Rel(cwd, ...) both assume cwd IS the working-tree root, but porcelain output is toplevel-relative regardless of cwd (verified empirically) and workspace.FindRoot exists precisely so next can run from a subdirectory. From a subdir of the anchor tree, every class disarms (samePath false) while the dirt is observable and the writes land in that tree — a default-config false negative; and had the gate passed, the Rel(cwd,...) paths ('../...') could never match toplevel-relative porcelain anyway. Both the gate comparison and the emitted relative paths must use the toplevel of cwd's tree, not cwd. Subsumed automatically by G-r2-1's preferred fix; add a subdir-invocation leg either way.

G-r2-3 (minor): Delete the stale first-draft doc block in ComputeEntangleablePaths. Lines ~94-116 of internal/next/guard.go still say the recording writes go 'ALWAYS ... under repoRoot (unconditionally — unlike the .gitignore write, this one does NOT route through resolveAnchorRoot)' and that the recording class gates on 'repoRoot == cwd' — both false: the code gates on samePath(anchor, cwd), and the corrected comment at lines ~132-137 (plus the RecordingEnabled pin's own doc comment) says SpecDir prefers the spec worktree copy. In a bead whose subject is state honesty, a self-contradicting derivation comment is a defect, not a cosmetic: fix it to describe the one true resolution (including whatever G-r2-1's disposition makes true).

findings.title: Recording-class observability gate diverges from the real write resolution under custom worktree_root
findings.detail: claimAnchorRoot replicates resolveAnchorRoot faithfully (verified line-by-line: SpecWorktreePath(root, cfg, specID) + os.Stat IsDir in both, mindspec_executor.go:1783-1801 vs guard.go:174-186). But the recording WRITES do not resolve through that preference: EventsPath/ManifestPath → workspace.SpecDir, whose worktree probes use DefaultWorktreesDir(root) with nil cfg — hardcoded '.worktrees' (worktree.go:104-116). cfg.WorktreeRoot is a real, validated config field (config.go:21,568-588). Custom worktree_root + recording enabled + spec worktree exists + invoked from repoRoot: write lands at repoRoot's spec dir (SpecDir fallback step 3), gate excludes the class (anchor==customWt != cwd), pre-existing dirty manifest.json at repoRoot proceeds as ignoredDirt and is then read-modify-written by AddBeadToPhase — round-1 F1's entanglement, alive in that config. The AC-8(ii) pins cannot catch it: both fixtures use the default '.worktrees'. Same mechanism for legacy-shaped trees (SpecDir's worktree probes cover flat/canonical only; legacy is probed under root alone, step 5). The failure direction is fail-open (proceed with notice), never a wrongful block.

findings.title: samePath(anchor, cwd) and Rel(cwd, ...) use cwd where the working-tree toplevel is the honest base
findings.detail: Verified empirically: `git -C <subdir> status --porcelain` reports toplevel-relative paths, so dirt anywhere in the tree is observable from any subdirectory — but the gate compares anchor against cwd literally, and workspace.FindRoot(cwd) explicitly supports subdirectory invocation. From a subdir of the anchor tree all entangleable classes disarm in the DEFAULT config while the claim's writes land in that very tree. The existing artifact exemption ('.beads/issues.jsonl') already relies on porcelain's toplevel-relative base, so the package's own conventions point at toplevel, not cwd. Closed for free by G-r2-1's derive-from-resolved-path fix.

findings.title: ComputeEntangleablePaths' doc block contradicts its own code and its own later comment
findings.detail: guard.go ~94-116 states the recording writes go unconditionally under repoRoot and the class gates on repoRoot == cwd; the code gates on samePath(anchor, cwd) and the comment at ~132-137 (and both e2e pins' doc comments, which describe catching exactly this 'naively assumed repoRoot' first draft) state the opposite. The stale text is the first draft's model surviving in the shipped derivation comment.

findings.detail: TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_EnumerationPin_RecordingEnabled run by this reviewer: PASS (141s), a real bd+git claim from within the spec worktree whose porcelain diff exactly matches ComputeEntangleablePaths' prediction (manifest.json RMW + events.ndjson creation, len==2 pinned). TestCheckDirtyTreeProportional_RecordingEnabledDirtyManifestBlocks and the other-spec ignored leg pass at unit level. The recording class is real, per-spec, recording.enabled-gated, and the pin would go red if a future claim step added an unpredicted tracked write in the fixture's configuration.

findings.title: Round-1 F2 resolved: the refusal path now has real end-to-end coverage
findings.detail: TestNextCmd_ClaimGuard_GitignoreVariantsRefuseByteIdentical run by this reviewer: PASS (381s, four variants — modified/deleted/renamed-away/symlinked). Each drives the REAL binary through next.go's blockingDirt branch ('cannot claim work' asserted) and proves the refusal is a byte-identical no-op (bd status, branches, worktrees, file bytes). The round-1 concern that a deleted refusal branch in next.go would be invisible no longer holds. parsePorcelainZ's rename ordering (new path first, then orig) matches real git -z output, reproduced independently in a scratch fixture.

findings.title: Round-1 F3 resolved beyond the ask: presence bit consumed, four distinguished outcomes
findings.detail: backfillExistingEpicPhase now backfills ONLY on present == false; present-but-invalid is left untouched with its own message steering to `mindspec repair phase` — refusing to overwrite a corrupt or forward-incompatible value with a guess is the right call and strictly safer than round 1's write. All TestBackfillExistingEpicPhase legs pass. The lock-interaction analysis from round 1 is unchanged and still clean (no reentrancy on ApproveSpec's path, no double-write, forward-only serialization).
